assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits. The discovery chain from proglucagon processing to the active peptide, its insulinotropic action and clinical pharmacology is clear, original and of very large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and GLP-2), Holst (physiology and human studies of GLP-1) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide forms) are the most defensible discovery trio. Knudsen's drug-development role is major but is more engineering of long-acting analogues; Habener is not on the supplied list. Credit boundaries between discovery and development are contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups and by large outcome trials over more than a decade; clinical use is widespread. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution, compared with Knudsen's development of the drugs, is the fairest third place is debatable.
Credit for the original peptide work involves others not on the list (my recollection, not verified here).
Committee preference for basic discovery over drug development is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a method to control defined cell types with millisecond light pulses and has reshaped circuit neuroscience and physiology, including motor circuits, and led to vision restoration efforts. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The discovery of channelrhodopsin function (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted approach) divide the credit. A trio of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann captures the tool plus its microbial-opsin origin, but excludes Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck, which is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for about two decades, with a very large literature. Clinical translation remains early, but as a research tool it is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Six credited names cannot fit a three-person prize; exclusion of Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck is contentious.
Priority disputes over first neuronal use are unresolved.
Therapeutic validation is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapies. The concept is clear, original and clinically validated.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T clinical translation with 4-1BB costimulation), Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and preclinical foundations) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified lymphocyte trials) form a reasonable trio. Contributions of Eshhar, Kuwana and others fall outside the supplied credit and may complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of follow-up show durable responses in blood cancers. Solid tumours remain unresolved and safety concerns persist, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Early-concept credit (for example Eshhar's chimeric receptors) is not represented.
Rosenberg's relative role against Eshhar-type claims is uncertain.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and toxicity may temper the perceived completeness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central controller of growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism is a foundational concept in cell physiology, with implications for cancer, ageing, diabetes and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined its growth-control role; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and its nutrient-sensing pathway; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin underpinned target identification. Others (for example Heitman and Movva, Sabers, Brown and Snyder on mTOR/FRAP) also contributed to identifying the target, so the set is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated, conserved and understood in considerable mechanistic depth. Clinical rapalogs are in use, though the anti-ageing and broader therapeutic claims are still developing.
uncertainties: Priority among the mammalian target-identification groups is disputed.
Schreiber's contribution is chemical biology rather than TOR itself.
Whether the committee sees the clinical payoff as sufficient is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a signalling pathway from the ER to the nucleus that adjusts the folding capacity of the cell, with consequences for secretory physiology, metabolic and degenerative disease and cancer. It is a clear conceptual discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently identified the Ire1/Hac1 mechanism in yeast, including the unconventional splicing of HAC1 mRNA, and are the natural pair. The supplied credit does not include Mori's and Walter's collaborators in the other branches (for example PERK and ATF6) which could be considered for completeness.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across species for about three decades; mechanisms are well understood. Disease-directed therapeutic translation is still limited.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would also want credit for the PERK and ATF6 branches is unclear.
Clinical impact is still emerging compared with other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and interferon production, and is relevant for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. The mechanism is clear and the work has had a broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, which is decisive; Barber identified STING. Other credited names (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) made real contributions, with Sun and Wu in the Chen laboratory, so a two-person prize is plausible but could be disputed.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been strongly confirmed in many laboratories, but therapeutic validation through STING agonists and antagonists in humans has largely not yet succeeded. Somewhat early for the clinic, though sound for the basic science.
uncertainties: Others, such as Vance and Tomasz, also contributed to STING or cyclic dinucleotide biology (from my recollection, not verified).
Limited clinical translation.
Competition with the 2011 innate immunity prize in terms of perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the BCR-ABL concept established targeted therapy of cancer, turning chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable disease. The clarity and the lasting effect on drug development in oncology are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (discovery of the compound programme), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Rowley's and others' earlier work on the Philadelphia chromosome lies outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of follow-up data and many follow-on kinase inhibitors. It is very mature, and one could argue that recognition is somewhat late rather than premature.
uncertainties: The committee may regard the field as more drug development than basic discovery.
Allocation among the Novartis chemists (for example Zimmermann) is not on this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade is clinically effective led to anti-TNF biologics that changed the treatment of many chronic inflammatory diseases. The finding is conceptually clear and has had a lasting effect.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly conducted the key mechanistic and clinical studies and are a natural pair. Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody engineering (for example Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias) fall outside the credit and could raise allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Validated over about 25 years by multiple agents and indications; it is very mature. Timeliness is a question, since the work is old.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the contribution as the disease-mechanism discovery or as drug development.
Credit for TNF itself and for antibody construction involves other scientists.
